title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors and industry practitioners to navigate EU asset management and fund regulation: applying UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II across the value chain, and assessing delegation, liquidity, depositaries, cross-border marketing, sustainability disclosures and DORA.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors and practitioners a clear map of how EU law regulates funds, their managers and their distribution, and where the main supervisory risks lie across the fund value chain. Participants leave able to determine which rules apply to a given structure, test arrangements for delegation, liquidity, leverage and depositaries, and anticipate how ESMA and national competent authorities will approach them.
sections.What It Covers: The EU regulatory architecture and fund value chain, the UCITS Directive, AIFMD and AIFMD II, specialist regimes for ELTIFs, money market funds and venture capital funds, MiFID II and MiFIR for managers and distributors, delegation, substance and depositaries, liquidity management tools, leverage and valuation, cross-border marketing and passporting, SFDR and sustainability, and DORA and supervisory convergence.
Intended Audience: Supervisors, authorisation and policy staff at national competent authorities covering funds and asset managers
Compliance, legal, risk and product staff at UCITS management companies, AIFMs, investment managers and distributors
Directors, depositary and fund administration staff who need a working map of the EU fund rulebook
Learning Objectives: Explain how EU fund regulation is made and determine which rules apply across the value chain
Apply the core requirements of UCITS, AIFMD and AIFMD II to funds and their managers
Assess delegation, substance and depositary arrangements against EU expectations
Evaluate liquidity management tools, leverage and valuation and what can go wrong
Apply the rules on cross-border marketing, passporting, MiFID II distribution and SFDR disclosures
Identify how DORA, ESMA convergence work and reform proposals are reshaping the sector
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies and break-out exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored for supervisors, managers or distributors.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of asset management, funds or their supervision is helpful. No legal background or prior knowledge of EU law is required.
Core Reading: Directive 2009/65/EC on undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (UCITS Directive)
Directive 2011/61/EU on Alternative Investment Fund Managers (AIFMD)
Directive (EU) 2024/927 amending the AIFMD and UCITS Directive on delegation, liquidity risk management, supervisory reporting, depositary services and loan origination (AIFMD II)
Regulation (EU) 2019/2088 on sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector (SFDR)

modules.title: EU Regulatory Architecture and the Fund Value Chain
modules.summary: Level-setting on investing, asset management and funds, how EU rules are made and layered with Member State requirements, and a framework for deciding which rules apply at each link of the value chain.
objectives: Explain directives, regulations, technical standards, guidelines and Q&As and how they interact
Map the fund value chain from product and distribution to management, operations and administration
Determine which EU rules apply by asking what, who and how
syllabus: What investing, asset management and an investment fund are
Level 1 to Level 3: the Commission, co-legislators, ESMA and national authorities
UCITS or AIF: the core classification and why managers choose each
Break-out: mapping supervisory risks to the value chain

modules.title: The UCITS Directive: Product, Manager and Investor Protection
modules.summary: Why the UCITS framework exists, what it requires of funds and management companies, and whether its product rules have been effective in preventing investor harm.
objectives: Explain the history and global reach of the UCITS brand
Apply eligible asset, diversification, borrowing and risk management rules
Analyse whether UCITS rules prevented harm in a recent fund failure case study
syllabus: From UCITS I to UCITS V and the role of the management company
Eligible assets, spread rules, derivatives and efficient portfolio management
Exchange-traded funds and other specialist UCITS
Case study: an illiquid UCITS suspension and its lessons

modules.title: The AIFM Directive and AIFMD II
modules.summary: How AIFMD regulates managers rather than products, the requirements for authorised and registered managers, and the changes introduced by AIFMD II on delegation, liquidity, loan origination and reporting.
objectives: Explain AIFMD's scope, thresholds and manager-level requirements
Identify the obligations on authorisation, risk management, remuneration and reporting
Assess the impact of AIFMD II on managers, funds and supervisors
syllabus: Why AIFMD was created and what it regulates
Authorised and sub-threshold managers, third-country managers and private placement
Reporting to supervisors and transparency to investors
AIFMD II: loan-originating funds, delegation reporting and changes to UCITS

modules.title: Specialist Fund Regimes: ELTIFs, MMFs and EuVECA
modules.summary: A short tour of the EU product regulations that sit on top of the UCITS and AIF classification, what each is designed to achieve and the supervisory issues each raises.
objectives: Explain the purpose and core rules of the ELTIF, MMF, EuVECA and EuSEF regimes
Distinguish CNAV, LVNAV and VNAV money market funds and their stability risks
Identify the retail access and liquidity questions raised by the revised ELTIF regime
syllabus: ELTIF and ELTIF 2.0: long-term investment and retail access
Money market funds: types, liquidity buffers and the reform debate
EuVECA and EuSEF: venture and social entrepreneurship funds
When a specialist label adds value and when it adds complexity

modules.title: MiFID II and MiFIR for Managers and Distributors
modules.summary: How MiFID II and MiFIR apply to portfolio managers, investment managers acting as delegates and fund distributors, including product governance, inducements, costs disclosure and transparency.
objectives: Explain where MiFID II applies across portfolio management and fund distribution
Apply product governance, suitability, appropriateness and inducement rules
Assess costs and charges disclosure from manufacturer to end investor
syllabus: Individual portfolio management and the delegated investment manager
Product governance: target market, distribution strategy and review
Inducements, costs and charges, and the PRIIPs key information document
MiFIR transparency and transaction reporting for managers

modules.title: Delegation, Substance and Depositaries
modules.summary: How managers delegate portfolio and risk management while retaining responsibility, what supervisors expect of substance, and the depositary's role in safekeeping, oversight and cash flow monitoring.
objectives: Assess delegation arrangements against EU rules and ESMA substance expectations
Identify letter-box risk and weak oversight of delegates
Explain depositary duties, liability and independence for UCITS and AIFs
syllabus: Delegation conditions, oversight of delegates and AIFMD II reporting
Substance: senior management, resources and the letter-box test
Depositary safekeeping, oversight and cash flow monitoring duties
Depositary liability, independence and conflicts of interest

modules.title: Liquidity Management Tools, Leverage and Valuation
modules.summary: How EU rules address liquidity mismatch, leverage and valuation in funds, the liquidity management tools now required of open-ended funds, and the red flags that precede fund suspensions and losses.
objectives: Explain liquidity stress testing and the selection and activation of liquidity management tools
Assess leverage measures, limits and reporting for UCITS and AIFs
Identify valuation governance weaknesses, especially for hard-to-value assets
syllabus: Liquidity mismatch, stress testing and ESMA guidelines
Liquidity management tools: swing pricing, anti-dilution levies, gates and suspensions
Leverage: gross and commitment methods, global exposure and supervisory limits
Valuation policies, independence and red flags

modules.title: Cross-Border Marketing, Passporting and Disclosure
modules.summary: How funds and managers operate across the single market through product and management passports, the cross-border distribution framework, and the disclosure and costs rules that protect investors.
objectives: Explain the UCITS and AIFMD marketing and management passports
Apply rules on pre-marketing, marketing communications and de-notification
Assess costs and charges against the prohibition on undue costs
syllabus: Home and host roles in fund and manager passporting
Cross-border distribution rules, pre-marketing and marketing communications
Investor classification: retail, professional and semi-professional access
Undue costs, fee supervision and value for money

modules.title: Sustainable Finance: SFDR and Greenwashing
modules.summary: How the EU sustainable finance framework applies to funds and managers, from SFDR classification and principal adverse impacts to fund naming rules, and whether disclosures prevent greenwashing.
objectives: Explain SFDR entity and product disclosures and the Article 6, 8 and 9 categories
Assess sustainability claims in fund documents, names and marketing
Evaluate the SFDR review and the case for product categories
syllabus: SFDR, the Taxonomy Regulation and sustainability preferences under MiFID II
Principal adverse impacts and pre-contractual and periodic templates
ESMA guidelines on fund names using ESG or sustainability terms
Break-out: spotting greenwashing and greenbleaching

modules.title: DORA, Supervisory Convergence and the Regulatory Horizon
modules.summary: Brings the programme together with the cross-cutting rules that reach asset managers indirectly, ESMA's convergence toolkit, and the reforms likely to shape fund regulation over the coming years.
objectives: Explain how DORA applies to UCITS management companies and AIFMs
Describe ESMA's convergence tools and how they shape national supervision
Identify the regulatory topics that will shape the sector and agree priorities
syllabus: DORA for asset managers: ICT risk, incidents and third-party providers
Other rules reaching funds: EMIR, short selling, AML and market abuse
ESMA Q&As, guidelines, peer reviews and common supervisory actions
Workshop: the reform horizon and a twelve-month priorities plan

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
related.summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
related.summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.

related.title: Digital Operational Resilience under DORA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on DORA for supervisors and financial entities: ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and TLPT, ICT third-party risk and critical provider oversight.

related.title: EU Payments Regulation: PSD2, PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on EU payments regulation for supervisors and firms, covering PSD2 and EMD2 today and the PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation reform package.
